channel.title: Responsible AI & Neurodivergence, Naba Rizvi
channel.description: Daily curated research feed on ethical and responsible AI, with emphasis on neurodivergent people and serious mental illness.

item.title: Evaluating large language models for assessment of psychosis risk
item.description: Eleven open weight models were asked to read 678 partial PSYCHS interview transcripts from 373 participants, most of them at clinical high risk for psychosis, and to infer risk status plus severity and frequency across fifteen symptom domains. The largest model reached 0.80 accuracy with 0.93 sensitivity but only 0.58 specificity, and generated symptom scores correlated well with researcher ratings. Clinically relevant confabulation stayed low at three percent, and the dominant error was over pathologising non clinical experiences, the direction that would push people into assessment they do not need. Performance held across most demographic groups but varied by site, so the case here is for human in the loop triage rather than autonomous screening.

item.title: AI supported therapeutic interventions for autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review
item.description: Five databases covering January 2016 to December 2025 yielded only fourteen studies in which an AI system moved past a proposed model into multi session use with diagnosed autistic participants. Robotics, virtual reality and wearables mostly functioned as a social mediator, with gains on ADOS and SRS scores attributed to reduced cognitive load, real time task adaptation and fine grained behavioural monitoring such as eye tracking. The limits are the story: dosage varied widely at a median of four to twelve hours, samples were typically under twenty participants and heavily male, and there were no adult participants in any included study. Claims about AI for autism care therefore rest on evidence drawn from a narrow slice of autistic people, with adults and the female phenotype absent.

item.title: NeuroBridge: using generative AI to bridge cross neurotype communication differences
item.description: Most cross neurotype interventions ask autistic people to adapt, so this platform inverts the burden by having a language model play a direct and literal conversational partner across four scenarios while a neurotypical user practises and receives feedback. Twelve neurotypical participants came away describing autism as a social difference that needs understanding from others, and rated the generated feedback as constructive, logical and non judgmental. The finding that should travel further is that most participants judged the simulated portrayal of autism to be accurate, which suggests users will readily accept AI generated misrepresentations of disability. Building perspective taking tools therefore means taking responsibility for whose version of autism the model is teaching.

item.title: FDA pilot lets generative AI medical devices reach patients before authorisation
item.description: Four devices, including products from Cadence and Limbic, have been accepted into the agency's TEMPO pilot, which allows digital health companies to put generative AI tools on the market without marketing authorisation. The stated purpose is to expand the pool of technologies available to the Medicare ACCESS model for chronic condition management, while giving regulators hands on experience with generative systems in real world settings. Limbic works in mental health, so this is a route by which conversational AI reaches psychiatric patients ahead of a formal authorisation decision. Whether provisional market access carries monitoring strong enough to catch the relational failure modes documented in the research literature is the open question.

item.title: HHS extends the Section 504 deadline for accessible web content and mobile apps
item.description: An interim final rule gives recipients of HHS funding another year to bring web content and mobile applications up to WCAG 2.1 AA under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, moving the date to May 2027 for organisations with fifteen or more employees and May 2028 for smaller ones. The department cites community health centres and hospitals that reported they could not meet the original deadline, and aligns the timeline with parallel Justice Department rulemaking under Title II of the ADA. Since patient facing AI increasingly arrives through the same portals and apps, this deadline sets the floor for whether disabled patients can reach those tools at all. The rule adds no new obligations and preserves current requirements, so the shift is in enforcement timing rather than in substance.
